security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, inline code, headings, and one public documentation link. No executable scripts, shell backtick execution, data exfiltration, prompt injection attempt, or system reconnaissance intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples trigger static security patterns.
remediation.suggestion: No security fix is required. Marketplace tooling may suppress these patterns when they appear only inside Markdown documentation.

remediation.issue: External checklist link appears as a network indicator.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the public reference link, or label it clearly as documentation if future review tooling supports annotations.

static_findings.snippet: - Working in a directory containing `.move` files or `Move.toml`
- Find all `.move` files using glob patterns
- ✅ GOOD when importing members: `use my_package::my_module::{Self, Member};`
- ❌ BAD: `const NOT_AUTHORIZED: u64 = 0;` (all-caps reserved for regular constants)
- ❌ BAD: `const MyConstant: vector<u8> = b"value";` (PascalCase suggests error)
- ✅ GOOD: `public struct AdminCap has key, store { id: UID }`
- ❌ BAD: `public struct Admin has key, store { id: UID }` (unclear it's a capability)
- ❌ BAD: `public struct PromisePotato {}` (redundant, abilities show it's hot potato)
- ✅ GOOD: `public struct UserRegistered has copy, drop { user: address }`
- ❌ BAD: `public struct RegisterUser has copy, drop { user: address }` (ambiguous)
- ✅ CANONICAL: `public struct DynamicFieldKey() has copy, drop, store;`
- ⚠️ ACCEPTABLE: `public struct DynamicField has copy, drop, store {}`
- ✅ GOOD: `public fun do_something(): T { ... }` (composable, returns value)
- ❌ BAD: `public fun mint_and_transfer(ctx: &mut TxContext) { transfer::transfer(...) }` (not compos
- ❌ BAD: `public fun authorize(cap: &AdminCap, app: &mut App)` (breaks method associativity)
- ✅ GOOD: `public fun details_mut(u: &mut User): &mut Details` (mutable accessor)
- ❌ BAD: `use std::string::utf8; let str = utf8(b"hello, world!");`
- ❌ BAD: `let mut my_vec = vector::empty(); vector::push_back(&mut my_vec, 10);`
- ✅ GOOD: `let sum = source.fold!(0, |acc, v| acc + v);`
- ✅ GOOD: `let filtered = source.filter!(|e| e > 10);` (requires T: drop)
- ❌ BAD: `let MyStruct { id, field_1: _, field_2: _, field_3: _ } = value;`
- ❌ BAD: Separate `#[test]` and `#[expected_failure]` on different lines
- ✅ GOOD: End with `abort` to show failure point
- ❌ BAD: Include `test.end()` or other cleanup in expected_failure tests
- ❌ BAD: `#[test] fun test_this_feature() { }` (redundant in test module)
- ✅ GOOD for simple tests: `let ctx = &mut tx_context::dummy();`
- ❌ BAD: `assert!(is_success, 0);` (may conflict with app error codes)
- ✅ GOOD: `assert_eq!(result, expected_value);` (shows both values on failure)
- **Testing** - Use simplest approach that works; avoid over-engineering

content.value_statement: Move teams need consistent reviews for Move 2024 syntax, package manifests, tests, and Sui patterns. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a structured checklist with prioritized feedback.
actual_capabilities: Checks Move.toml edition, dependencies, and named address conventions.
Reviews module syntax, imports, constants, structs, and event naming.
Evaluates function visibility, composability, parameter order, and getter names.
Compares Move code against modern method, macro, and collection patterns.
Reviews test style, assertion usage, cleanup behavior, and comment conventions.
Produces prioritized findings with file references, impact, and recommended fixes.
limitations: It provides review guidance and does not compile or execute Move packages by itself.
It depends on the assistant reading the relevant project files before reporting.
It focuses on code quality and style, not formal verification or exploit detection.
Recommendations assume current Move 2024 and Sui framework conventions.

use_cases.title: Audit a Move Package
use_cases.description: Review a package before release for manifest issues, outdated syntax, weak tests, and non-composable APIs.

use_cases.title: Improve Pull Request Quality
use_cases.description: Use a repeatable checklist to give contributors clear feedback on Move 2024 style and Sui best practices.

use_cases.title: Learn Modern Move Patterns
use_cases.description: Compare existing code with recommended examples for modules, functions, macros, tests, and comments.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Move File
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a specific source file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Move file for code quality. Focus on Move 2024 syntax, naming, function signatures, and clear fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Review Package Manifest
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Move.toml against the Move Book checklist. Check edition, dependencies, and named addresses.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Package Before Merge
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review across a full package.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Move package for code quality before merge. Prioritize critical issues, important improvements, and recommended enhancements.

prompt_templates.title: Deep Review With Fix Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review that prepares implementation work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a full Move 2024 quality review. Group findings by category, explain impact, and create an ordered fix plan.

output_examples.input: Review a Move package that has no edition in Move.toml and uses legacy module braces.
output: Summary with critical manifest and syntax issues first.
Findings that cite the manifest and source files with clear impact.
Recommended edits that add Move 2024 edition and modern module labels.

output_examples.input: Check a Move test module for quality issues.
output: Feedback on test names, expected failure attributes, cleanup behavior, and assertions.
A prioritized list of changes that improves clarity without overengineering tests.

output_examples.input: Ask whether a public entry function should return an object instead.
output: Explanation of composability tradeoffs for programmable transaction blocks.
Recommendation for a public function or entry function based on the intended use.

best_practices: Ask for the package scope before running a broad review.
Start with Move.toml because edition and dependency issues affect many checks.
Report findings with file references, impact, and a concrete fix.
anti_patterns: Do not treat style advice as a substitute for compiling and testing the package.
Do not apply all recommendations without checking project context.
Do not use the skill for security assurance without a separate security review.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews Move packages against the Move Book Code Quality Checklist and Move 2024 conventions.

faq.question: Does it support Sui projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance includes Sui framework patterns, package dependencies, objects, capabilities, and testing conventions.

faq.question: Can it fix issues automatically?
faq.answer: It can propose fixes and guide edits when the assistant has permission to modify files.

faq.question: Does it replace unit tests?
faq.answer: No. It improves review consistency, but users should still compile, test, and verify the package.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The skill is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code in the report metadata.

faq.question: Is it focused on security?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on code quality and style. Security review should be performed separately.
